lessons.title: Story Time: 'Pirates Love Underpants' or Similar Pirate Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe the pirates' quest in the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read a fun pirate-themed story, discussing what the pirates are searching for.
key_questions: What are the pirates looking for?

differentiation.extension: Retell part of the story in own words

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and engagement — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite part of the story.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Counting Treasure Coins
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count treasure coin counters accurately up to 10+.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a pile of gold coin counters together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and sort treasure coins into treasure chests, recording totals.
resources_needed: Coin counters, small boxes as treasure chests
key_questions: Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class total treasure count.
lessons.home_link: Count coins or small objects at home together.

lessons.title: What Is a Map?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain simply what a map shows.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple treasure map example.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss what a map is for and how symbols represent real things (X marks the spot, trees, water).
key_questions: What does a map show us?

differentiation.extension: Explain how a map key works

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early map-reading understanding — evidence for UTW.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap what a map shows.
lessons.home_link: Look at a map together at home (real or online).

lessons.title: Making a Treasure Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create their own simple treasure map with symbols.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the map discussion from UTW.
lessons.main_activity: Children design their own pirate treasure map, adding symbols for landmarks and marking an 'X' for treasure.
resources_needed: Paper (aged with tea-staining optional), pens, crayons

differentiation.extension: Add a key explaining each symbol

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe creative design and symbolic representation — evidence for EAD.1/UTW.1.
lessons.plenary: Display treasure maps together.
lessons.home_link: Make a simple treasure map for a game at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Consolidation - Reading Pirate Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple pirate-themed words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned this year.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading pirate-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the ship has a flag').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading pirate words over the week.

lessons.title: Following a Treasure Map: Positional Language
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow directional instructions to find hidden treasure.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap positional/directional language from Week 22.
lessons.main_activity: Using a simple floor map with markers, children follow step-by-step directions to find 'hidden treasure'.
resources_needed: Floor map/masking tape path, hidden treasure marker
key_questions: Which way do we go now?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note directional language understanding — evidence for MATHS.2/CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate finding the treasure together.
lessons.home_link: Set up a simple treasure hunt with directions at home.

lessons.title: How Do Compasses Work? (Simple Introduction)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say simply that a compass helps you find directions.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real or picture compass.
lessons.main_activity: Simple exploration of a compass, discussing that it always points north and helps travellers/pirates find their way.
key_questions: Why might a pirate need one?

differentiation.extension: Try using the compass to find north in the room

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative engagement with a navigation tool — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what a compass is for.
lessons.home_link: Look at a compass (or compass app) together at home.

lessons.title: Pirate Role-Play and Ship Adventure
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to engage in imaginative pirate role-play using props.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise saying 'ahoy' and other pirate phrases.
lessons.main_activity: Free role-play in a pirate ship corner (chairs/boxes as a ship), taking on captain and crew roles with imaginative pirate language.
resources_needed: Pirate role-play props, eye patches, hats

differentiation.extension: Child extends the scenario with own ideas

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative role-play and language — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Share the adventures had today.
lessons.home_link: Play a pretend pirate adventure at home.

lessons.title: Writing 'X Marks the Spot' Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write simple map labels.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Monday's treasure map craft.
lessons.main_activity: Children add written labels to their treasure map (e.g. 'X', 'sea', 'ship') using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What label do you need here?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note purposeful writing attempt — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled maps with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Add labels to your home-made map.

lessons.title: Shapes on the Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify 2D shapes used as map symbols.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at Monday's maps and identify shapes used.
lessons.main_activity: Children design map symbols using given 2D shape stencils (triangle mountain, square chest), naming each shape.

differentiation.extension: Combine 4+ shapes and name them all

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition and symbolic application — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display map symbol designs.
lessons.home_link: Look for shapes used as symbols (road signs) at home.

lessons.title: Pirates Long Ago
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say that pirates existed a long time ago.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the concept of 'long ago' from the dinosaurs topic.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss simply that real pirates lived hundreds of years ago, sailing ships and sometimes finding treasure, distinguishing fact from the fun stories.
key_questions: Did pirates live long ago or now?
What do you think their ships were like?

differentiation.extension: Compare pirate ships to modern ships

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early historical understanding — evidence for UTW.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap that pirates are part of history.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fact about pirates in history together.

lessons.title: Making a Pirate Ship Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a pirate ship model using materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of pirate ships.
lessons.main_activity: Children build a pirate ship using a cardboard box/boat shape, adding a paper sail and flag.
resources_needed: Cardboard boxes, paper, sticks, craft materials
key_questions: How did you make the sail?

differentiation.extension: Design own flag and additional details

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe construction planning and material joining skill — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display pirate ships together as a 'fleet'.
lessons.home_link: Build a boat using recycling at home.

lessons.title: Retelling the Pirate Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the story from Monday.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words and pirate ship props.
resources_needed: Story sequencing cards, pirate ship craft
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Recap: Treasure Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 using a treasure-themed activity.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire number bonds to 10 quiz.
lessons.main_activity: Using coin counters split between two treasure chests, children practise and record all number bonds to 10.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Class Treasure Hunt (Using Our Maps)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a map to find a hidden object.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap how to read the maps made this week.
lessons.main_activity: Using their own or a class treasure map, children follow it around the outdoor/indoor space to find hidden 'treasure'.
resources_needed: Maps from the week, hidden treasure (stickers/tokens)
key_questions: Where does the map say to go next?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note practical application of map-reading skills — evidence for UTW.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate finding the treasure together.
lessons.home_link: Follow a simple map or set of directions at home.

lessons.title: Pirate Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sing a pirate-themed song with actions.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap pirate role-play from Tuesday.
lessons.main_activity: Learn a simple pirate-themed song with actions, performing with confidence.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe participation and expressive movement — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the song once more.
lessons.home_link: Sing the pirate song for family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: Pirate-Themed Reading Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read pirate-themed sentences fluently.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading a range of pirate-themed sentences with increasing fluency.
key_questions: Can you read it more quickly?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note reading fluency progress — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading pirate sentences over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Position, Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, positional language, and shape skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting treasure coins, following map directions, map symbol shapes.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 34 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and directions over the weekend.

lessons.title: Pirates and Maps Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about pirates and maps learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Pirates and Maps' display combining maps, ships, and compass learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about pirates and maps?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about pirates and maps with your family.

lessons.title: Pirates and Maps Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform the pirate song and a mini treasure hunt scene with confidence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining the pirate song and a short treasure hunt re-enactment, with ships and maps displayed.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the pirates and maps week.
lessons.home_link: Perform the pirate song for family this weekend.
